text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Australian engraver and printer JOHN SANDS was born in 1818. His first Christmas card depicted a little girl offering a Christmas pudding to a swaggie.
Russian composer ALEXANDER PORFIREVICH BORODIN, who was also a professor of chemistry and medicine, was born in 1834. He
was best-known for the opera "Prince Igor". His tunes were used in the musical "Kismet".
French sculptor AUGUSTE RODIN, who specialised in realism, was born in 1840.

American actress GRACE KELLY, the Hollywood star who became a real-life princess, was born in 1929. She married Prince Rainier of Monaco in 1956 after a brief career as an actress. She co-starred with GARY COOPER in "High Noon" in 1952. Her final movie was "High Society" with BING CROSBY and FRANK SINATRA. She died in September 1982 in a car crash.
Romanian gymnast NADIA COMANECI, who won three Olympic gold medals at the age of 14, was born in 1961. Upon retirement she became a coach of the Romanian team, but defected to Canada in 1989.

Canadian singer, songwriter and guitarist NEIL YOUNG was born in 1945. After several high school rock bands he formed the 'Mynah Birds'. NEIL released his first solo album in 1969 just before joining 'Crosby, Stills, Nash and Young'. Hits included "Woodstock" (1970), "Teach Your Children" (1970) and "Ohio" (1970). He also released records as 'NEIL YOUNG and Crazy Horse'. His solo career continued and as recently as 1991 his LP "WELD" was lauded.

British singer, songwriter with 'Hot Chocolate' ERROL BROWN was born in 1948. The biggest hits include "You Sexy Thing" (1975), "So You Win Again" (1977) and "No Doubt About It" (1978). IN 1987 ERROL started his solo career and had success with "Personal Touch".
** EVENTS **
1847 : A new anaesthetic called chloroform was

demonstrated publicly for the first time. Professor at the University of Edinburgh Sir JAMES SIMPSON said the new chemical had three times the potency of ether. He praised its application particularly for use during childbirth. The public trial drew immediate criticism from Scottish Calvinists who opposed all use of anaesthetics in childbirth as against the will of God.
1901 : Gales swept Britain killing 200 and capsizing many
ships.
1905 : The Russian occupation imposed martial law on
Poland.
1918 : The British House of Commons voted for a war loan
of 1295 million dollars, bringing its war debts to more than 13,000 million dollars.
1919 : The first flight from England to Australia began

in London. KEITH and ROSS SMITH took off with their mechanics BENNET and SHIERS in a flying race. They landed in Darwin after covering 18,500 kilometres in 27 days and 20 hours. Australia's Prime Minister BILLY HUGHES had offered 10,000 pounds to the first Australian crew to make the flight in less than 720 hours. The SMITH brothers' actual flying time was 135 hours 50 minutes.
1933 : The first photograph of the supposed Loch Ness
monster was taken by HUGH GRAY. He managed to take five photographs before Nessie slipped from view. Four were blank and the fifth showed an object that looked like a tree trunk.
1942 : The British Eighth Army under General BERNARD
MONTGOMERY captured Tobruk, Libya, taking at least 30,000 prisoners.
1944 : The German battleship Tirpitz, sister ship of the
Bismarck and Hitler's last major warship, was sunk by Lancaster bombers at Tromso Fjord in northern Norway.
1948 : A war crimes tribunal in Japan passed death

sentences on former prime minister General HIDEKI TOJO and six colleagues on charges of breaching the laws and customs of war. 1954 : More than 15,000 people caused a near riot in Melbourne at an appearance of United States cowboy star WILLIAM BOYD as Hopalong Cassidy.
1963 : ROBERT MENZIES became the first Australian Prime
Minister to deliver his policy speech on television.
1974 : A mysterious car crash claimed the life of KAREN
SILKWOOD. She had been working at the KERR McGEE nuclear plant and was investigating irregularities.
1974 : Australian Prime Minister GOUGH WHITLAM announced
tax cuts of 650 million dollars to stimulate the economy.
1979 : Australian cricketer IAN CHAPPELL was suspended
for three weeks for using abusive language in a Shield match in Devonport.
1987 : Moscow Communist Party leader BORIS YELTSIN was
fired by President GORBACHEV after YELTSIN was critical of the slow pace of perestroika (reconstruction).
1988 : West Indies cricket captain VIV RICHARDS scored
his 100th century at a game in Sydney.
1990 : Iraq gave Kuwaitis until November 25 to take up

Iraqi identity cards. The ultimatum followed the Iraq invasion of Kuwait in August which led to the Gulf War in early 1991. The United Kingdom, United States, Australia, France and Egypt sent troops to repel the invaders. The air offensive lasting six weeks destroyed about one-third of Iraqi equipment and inflicted massive casualties.
1990 : A demonstration in Paris involving more than
20,000 children turned into a riot. The children were demanding a better education.
1995 : Serbs abandoned a four-year separatist revolt in
Croatia, signing an accord to hand over the strategic Eastern Slavonia region and lifting the threat of fighting that could have wrecked peace hopes in the Balkans.
